Class ClassToBuild

Object
ClassToBuild
public class ClassToBuild extends Object
The standard Builder pattern is used when objects of a ClassToBuild require multiple steps. The "build"- methods are encapsulated in a separate Builder-class that is often included in the ClassToBuild (part-of).

The ClassToBuild has a static method called builder() that returns an instance of the Builder-class. Objects of the Builder-class encapsulate the state of the build process for each object-to-build.

Build methods are often chainable. The chain ends with the build()-method that creates the actual object-to-build ending the build process.

The implementation of the strict Singleton pattern: 

public class ClassToBuild {

    public static class Builder {

        public Builder step_1() {
             return this;
        }
        public Builder step_2() {
             return this;
        }
        public Builder step_3() {
             return this;
        }
  
        public ClassToBuild build() {
             return new ClassToBuild();
        }
    }

    public static Builder builder() {
        return new Builder();
    }
}
